digests.why_two_flavours_are_pinned: threat detection engine's kept half is 'fed from files/journald', and the pinned image README is explicit that journalctl support exists only in the debian build ('The debian version includes support for systemd and journalctl', flavours `crowdsecurity/crowdsec:{version}-debian`). The alpine digest is the default because it is the production flavour upstream recommends; the debian digest is here so the journald half of threat detection engine is a one-value change and not a scavenger hunt. Neither has been pulled.
digests.why_slim_is_recorded_but_not_recommended: `slim` drops the notification plugins (image README: 'it does not include the notifier plugins nor the GeoIP database'), and the HTTP plugin is the entire inbound path this component uses, so `slim` cannot deliver a CrowdSec alert to the platform. Recording the digest is the difference between 'unavailable' and 'available and wrong for this purpose'.
digests.verified_by: sha256 of the manifest bytes returned by the registry, compared to the digest used to request them (self-hash), not to a tag page that asserted it

digest_provenance.method: This repository's own resolver, scripts/resolve_images.py::resolve (the same function that pins the platform stage's images): an anonymous pull token from https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=repository:crowdsecurity/crowdsec:pull, GET the manifest by tag with an Accept covering the OCI index and Docker manifest-list types, take the single linux/amd64 entry of that index, re-fetch it by digest, and verify each returned Docker-Content-Digest equals sha256 of the bytes it came with. Every value came from a GET: the registry answers HEAD on /manifests/ with 405 unless an Accept header is sent.
digest_provenance.resolved_with: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from resolve_images import resolve; print(resolve('crowdsecurity/crowdsec:v1.8.1'))" -> {'source_index_digest': 'sha256:0f2523fa...', 'image': 'crowdsecurity/crowdsec@sha256:dd16bad0...', 'platform': 'linux/amd64'} on 2026-09-09; :v1.8.1-debian and :v1.8.1-slim returned the pairs above; :latest returned the identical index and amd64 digests as v1.8.1.
